item.title: Diwali spirit spreads joy to 100 vulnerable families through festive donations
item.description: The spirit of giving and kindness is shining bright this Diwali, with 100 packages prepared for vulnerable families across Lautoka to ensure they too can enjoy the festival of lights. Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka resident Narayan Reddy says 80 packages were prepared through local contributions, while another 20 were funded by his brother who lives in Australia.
item.content:encoded:
The spirit of giving and kindness is shining bright this Diwali, with 100 packages prepared for vulnerable families across Lautoka to ensure they too can enjoy the festival of lights.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Lautoka resident Narayan Reddy says 80 packages were prepared through local contributions, while another 20 were funded by his brother who lives in Australia.

Reddy says each package includes food, prepared sweets, items for Diwali Pooja and six bottles of drinking water to help families, particularly those facing water shortages.

He says the initiative has been running for about five years and was inspired by conversations he used to have with his late friend, Allen Lockington about helping families during Diwali and Christmas.

Reddy says they continue to honour that tradition by distributing packages to between 80 and 100 families during the festive seasons.

He says preparations for the packages took about one to two weeks.

He says while some families have everything they need to celebrate Diwali, others struggle to afford even the basic items.

Reddy is encouraging people to share what they have, support vulnerable families and ensure everyone gets an opportunity to celebrate Diwali.

item.title: Fuel costs rise by nearly $300M for Fiji Airways, another loss expected - Scurrah
item.description: Fiji Airways is expected to record another financial loss in 2026 as the airline faces nearly $300 million in additional fuel costs due to the volatility in fuel prices compared to last year. CEO and Managing Director Paul Scurrah revealed this during fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, saying the airline continues to face significant financial challenges, with fuel prices having more th
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Airways is expected to record another financial loss in 2026 as the airline faces nearly $300 million in additional fuel costs due to the volatility in fuel prices compared to last year.

CEO and Managing Director Paul Scurrah revealed this during fijivillage Straight Talk with Vijay Narayan, saying the airline continues to face significant financial challenges, with fuel prices having more than doubled compared to 2025.

Scurrah says although Fiji Airways has not finalised its financial results for 2026, he would not be surprised if the airline records another loss.

He says rising fuel prices are affecting airlines around the world, forcing Fiji Airways to review its spending and make difficult decisions to remain financially sustainable.

Scurrah says the airline also continues to carry significant debt and accumulated losses from the COVID-19 pandemic, making the current fuel crisis even more challenging.

He says Fiji Airways could have cut flights and grounded aircraft to reduce its losses, but such a decision would have had serious consequences for Fiji's tourism industry and the wider economy.

Scurrah says approximately 70 percent of visitors to Fiji travel on Fiji Airways, and reducing flights would affect businesses and jobs that depend on tourism.

He says this is why the airline approached the Government for financial support to maintain its flight operations.

Scurrah explains that the Government's $200 million loan guarantee is not a direct cash payment to Fiji Airways, but provides security for borrowing from financial institutions.

He also reveals that the new 5 percent tourism tax is expected to generate approximately $48 million for the airline this year.

Scurrah says the revenue will help offset some of the additional fuel costs, although Fiji Airways will still have to absorb most of the increase.

He says the airline has developed a five-year plan to return to sustainable profitability and is reviewing its operating costs, investments and business structure.

Scurrah adds that Fiji Airways is also strengthening its fuel hedging programme to better manage future fuel price fluctuations.

Despite the financial challenges, he says the airline remains committed to maintaining flights and supporting Fiji's tourism industry.

Scurrah stresses that the decisions being made now are aimed at ensuring Fiji Airways remains financially strong and sustainable in the years ahead.

item.title: Granddaughter of prominent Lautoka resident set to make history in NZ politics
item.description: Qiulae Wong, the granddaughter of prominent Lautoka resident Eddie Wong, is on track to lead New Zealand's Opportunity Party into Parliament for the first time following a strong showing in Saturday's general election. In the 1940s, Qiulae Wong's grandfather, Eddie Wong established Lukbo as a range of beverages manufactured by his company, Eddie Hin Limited in Lautoka.
item.content:encoded:
Qiulae Wong, the granddaughter of prominent Lautoka resident Eddie Wong, is on track to lead New Zealand's Opportunity Party into Parliament for the first time following a strong showing in Saturday's general election.

In the 1940s, Qiulae Wong's grandfather, Eddie Wong established Lukbo as a range of beverages manufactured by his company, Eddie Hin Limited in Lautoka.

For several decades, Eddie Hin Limited was a leading distributor, manufacturer, and retailer of food and beverages in Fiji, until Eddie's untimely passing in 1992.

As Mayor of Lautoka City, Eddie was a strong advocate for improving outcomes for the local community and played a key role in supporting the settlement of many Chinese migrant families in Fiji.

He also served as a Senator in the Fijian Government and was awarded a Member of the British Empire (MBE) in 1970 in recognition of his service.

Qiulae Wong who leads the Opportunity Party, has told supporters that the party is set to make history after nearly a decade of campaigning for New Zealand parliamentary representation.

With nearly 50 percent of votes counted on election night, the party had secured more than five percent of the votes counted at that stage, putting it on course to cross the threshold required to enter Parliament.

Early results indicated that the Opportunity Party could secure six to seven seats, potentially positioning it to play an important role in determining who forms New Zealand's next government.

Addressing supporters, Wong welcomed the result and thanked the party's candidates, volunteers and supporters for their commitment over the years.

She says voters have chosen unity over division and demonstrated their desire for change in New Zealand politics.

Wong says the result means a great deal to everyone who has worked towards the party's goal of securing representation in Parliament.

She stresses that while the party's breakthrough may appear to have happened overnight, it is the result of nearly a decade of hard work.

The projected result also carries a special connection to Fiji through Wong's family ties to Lautoka.

The final election results are yet to be confirmed.

item.title: Chaudhry urges Fijians to strengthen national unity this Diwali
item.description: Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry says the country must prioritise the hardships facing people amid political uncertainty and the ongoing drought. In his Diwali message, Chaudhry says the festival has, for well over a century, brought Fijians of different ethnicities and backgrounds together, making it a proud national celebration.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry says the country must prioritise the hardships facing people amid political uncertainty and the ongoing drought.

In his Diwali message, Chaudhry says the festival has, for well over a century, brought Fijians of different ethnicities and backgrounds together, making it a proud national celebration.

He says Fiji's multi-ethnic unity has always been one of the country's greatest strengths.

Chaudhry says this Diwali comes at a time when the country is facing political turbulence over the constitutional amendment process, as well as a crippling drought.

He says addressing the hardships faced by people must take priority over political manoeuvres to push through what he describes as an unpopular constitutional amendment.

Chaudhry is urging Fijians to reject divisive politics, stand together and work towards equality and national progress.

He is also reminding people to take extra care during Diwali celebrations, particularly when using fireworks and open flames, given the dry weather and drought conditions.

Chaudhry has wished all Fijians a peaceful Diwali with their loved ones and called for Lord Ram's blessings on the nation.

item.title: Put aside political differences and help those in need this Diwali – Prasad
item.description: As families across Fiji celebrate Diwali today, National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Prasad is urging people to put aside their political differences and remember those struggling with the rising cost of living and ongoing dry conditions. In his Diwali message, Professor Prasad says many families are facing financial difficulties and may not be able to celebrate the Festival of Lights
item.content:encoded:
As families across Fiji celebrate Diwali today, National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Prasad is urging people to put aside their political differences and remember those struggling with the rising cost of living and ongoing dry conditions.

In his Diwali message, Professor Prasad says many families are facing financial difficulties and may not be able to celebrate the Festival of Lights in the same way as others.

He says Diwali is a time to show kindness, share what people have and support those in need.

Professor Prasad also raises concerns about the drought affecting communities across Fiji and encourages people to check on neighbours who may be struggling with water shortages and other difficulties.

He says Fiji's cultural and religious diversity should bring people together rather than divide them.

Professor Prasad stresses that political differences should never damage friendships or relationships within communities.

He says Fiji has experienced enough division in its history, and people must work together to build a country where everyone feels respected and safe.

The NFP Leader is encouraging Fijians to use Diwali as an opportunity to rebuild friendships, settle differences and support families facing hardship.

Prasad says the true message of Diwali is about kindness, respect, unity and looking after one another.

He has also extended his Diwali greetings to everyone celebrating, wishing families peace, happiness, good health and prosperity.

item.title: Rabuka extends warm Diwali wishes to Hindus across Fiji
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has extended his warmest wishes to Hindus across Fiji as they celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights. Rabuka says he hopes this special occasion brings happiness, peace, good health and prosperity to families
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has extended his warmest wishes to Hindus across Fiji as they celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights.

Rabuka says he hopes this special occasion brings happiness, peace, good health and prosperity to families

He says the light of Diwali should inspire people to spread kindness, compassion and love while reminding everyone of the importance of living together in harmony and understanding.

The Prime Minister wishes everyone a Happy Diwali on behalf of his family.

item.title: FCCC urges families to prioritise food and fireworks safety this Diwali
item.description: As Fiji celebrates Diwali today, the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission is urging families to prioritise safety around fireworks and open flames while reminding shoppers to check food expiry dates and prices. In its Diwali message, FCCC says families should enjoy the Festival of Lights while taking precautions to protect their loved ones.
item.content:encoded:
As Fiji celebrates Diwali today, the Fijian Competition and Consumer Commission is urging families to prioritise safety around fireworks and open flames while reminding shoppers to check food expiry dates and prices.

In its Diwali message, FCCC says families should enjoy the Festival of Lights while taking precautions to protect their loved ones.

The Commission is reminding shoppers to check food expiry dates and packaging before purchasing items during the festive period.

FCCC is also encouraging consumers to check their receipts to ensure they are being charged the correct prices.

Meanwhile, the Commission is urging families to exercise extra caution when handling fireworks, diyas and candles amid ongoing dry conditions.

FCCC says parents and guardians must closely supervise children around fireworks and open flames and ensure they watch fireworks displays from a safe distance.

The Commission says Diwali is a time for families to come together and show kindness, fairness and respect for one another.

FCCC is encouraging everyone to celebrate responsibly, look after their neighbours and make safety a priority.

The Commission has also extended its Diwali greetings to families across Fiji and around the world, wishing everyone peace, good health and prosperity.

item.title: Diwali brings hope and togetherness to families in Bocalevu
item.description: The spirit of Diwali is bringing hope, love and togetherness to families in Bocalevu, Labasa, as residents come together to celebrate the festival of lights today. Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Nirijan Prasad says Diwali is one of the biggest and most important celebrations in the Hindu religion, representing love, care, forgiveness and unity.
item.content:encoded:
The spirit of Diwali is bringing hope, love and togetherness to families in Bocalevu, Labasa, as residents come together to celebrate the festival of lights today.

Speaking to fijivillage News, resident Nirijan Prasad says Diwali is one of the biggest and most important celebrations in the Hindu religion, representing love, care, forgiveness and unity.

Prasad says the festival is a time to put differences aside, forgive one another and spread love regardless of race or background.

He says although the drought has dried up local water sources, making preparations difficult, the Water Authority of Fiji delivered water to help families get ready for the celebrations.

He thanked the Authority for its assistance, saying sweets have been prepared and homes are ready for Diwali.

Prasad says families are now looking forward to the Diwali Pooja this afternoon and has wished everyone a happy and blessed Diwali.
